rule.title: Debugging Ansible Playbooks on OpenShift with ITZ Deployer
rule.description: Guide for debugging Ansible playbooks running in OpenShift with the IBM TechZone Deployer operator. When the Deployer operator provisions a deployment, it creates an Ansible job in the default namespace. This rule helps users locate and inspect job logs when troubleshooting playbook execution issues.

context.when_to_use: - User is debugging Ansible playbook execution in OpenShift - User reports Ansible job failures or unexpected behavior - User needs to inspect Ansible playbook logs - User is troubleshooting ITZ Deployer operator issues - User asks about finding Ansible job output or logs
context.architecture: IBM TechZone Deployer Operator (openshift-operators namespace) │ ▼ Ansible Job (default namespace) │ ▼ Job Pod Logs ◄──── Primary debugging location

step.title: Check the Ansible Job in the Default Namespace
step.description: The Ansible job runs in the 'default' namespace. Start by checking if the job exists and reviewing its pod logs.

web_console_method.navigation: 1. Open the OpenShift web console 2. Navigate to: Workloads > Jobs > Project: default 3. Look for a job associated with your deployment 4. Click the job name 5. Select the Pods tab to view the running or completed pod 6. Click the pod name 7. Select the Logs tab 8. Review the Ansible output for task failures, errors, or skipped steps
web_console_method.tip: Use the Download button in the Logs tab to save the full log output if it is too long to read in the console.

cli_method.commands:
# List Ansible jobs in the default namespace oc get jobs -n default
# Get the pod created by the job (replace with your job name) oc get pods -n default -l job-name=
# Stream the pod logs oc logs -n default -l job-name= --tail=-1

step.what_to_look_for: - Task failures or errors in the Ansible output - Skipped steps that should have executed - Variable values that may be incorrect - Connection or authentication errors - Resource creation failures

step.title: Job Not Found — Check the Deployer Operator Logs
step.description: If no Ansible job exists in the default namespace, the deployer operator controller may have encountered an error before the job could be created. The operator runs in the openshift-operators namespace.

web_console_method.navigation: 1. Navigate to: Workloads > Pods > Project: openshift-operators 2. Filter for a pod with 'itz-deployer-operator' in the name 3. Click the pod name 4. Select the Logs tab 5. Review for errors related to job creation

cli_method.commands:
# Find the deployer operator pod oc get pods -n openshift-operators | grep itz-deployer-operator
# Stream the operator logs (replace with the actual pod name) oc logs -n openshift-operators --tail=200

step.what_to_look_for: - Errors related to job creation - Permission or RBAC issues - Configuration validation failures - Resource quota or limit errors - API server connection issues

row.symptom: Ansible playbook failed or produced unexpected output

issue.cause: Cannot pull the Ansible runner image
issue.solution: Check image registry credentials and network connectivity

issue.cause: Ansible playbook has syntax errors or fails immediately
issue.solution: Review pod logs for Ansible syntax errors or missing dependencies

issue.symptom: Job completes but resources not created
issue.cause: Playbook tasks may be skipping or failing silently
issue.solution: Check pod logs for skipped tasks and verify variable values

issue.symptom: No job appears in default namespace
issue.cause: Operator controller failed before creating the job
issue.solution: Check deployer operator logs in openshift-operators namespace

best_practices.practice: Always check the Ansible job pod logs first — this is where playbook execution output appears
Use 'oc logs --tail=-1' to see the complete log output, not just recent lines
Download logs from the web console if they are too long to read in the browser
If the job doesn't exist, immediately check the operator controller logs
Look for the job name pattern that matches your deployment name

mcp_integration.note:
When users need to debug OpenShift-based Ansible deployments, you can use the openshift-mcp server to programmatically retrieve logs and resource information:
- use_mcp_tool with server_name="openshift-mcp" and tool_name="list_pods" to find Ansible job pods - use_mcp_tool with server_name="openshift-mcp" and tool_name="get_pod_logs" to retrieve logs - use_mcp_tool with server_name="openshift-mcp" and tool_name="list_jobs" to list Ansible jobs - use_mcp_tool with server_name="openshift-mcp" and tool_name="describe_resource" for detailed job info
